summary: Perry County, MO: 100-foot steel tower built about 1965 by the state conservation department; use ended in the 1980s and climbing is barred today.

access.note: 2018 plan: picnic area with limited public use; tower in caretaker status and prohibited from climbing until restoration plans are complete

facts.agency: Perry County, which took the site over from the Missouri Department of Conservation (deed 2022-23 per NHLR)

events.note: Missouri Department of Conservation erected the tower in fiscal 1964-65; the Register says circa 1965
Use ended in the 1980s; the Register gives no year, so 1980 marks only the start of that decade
Perry County commission began talks with the Department about taking over the site
Site deeded to Perry County for historical purposes; the Register dates this to 2022-23
Registered January 2, 2026; nominated by Jerry Lutes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2018 MDC plan still lists the site under Department responsibility; the NHLR says the county has administered it since the 2022-23 deed. The deed explains the change.

sources.title: Commissioners begin dialogue on fire tower

notes_for_editor: History and register facts agree with the record (built c.1965, standing, registered 2026, coordinates). Height 100 ft is taken from the 2021 report's cab-entrance height and converted to 30.5 m. Access is set to restricted: the 2018 plan gives the picnic area limited public use, and the tower is closed to climbing. Staffing is recorded as unknown because no source says whether the tower is staffed. The newest firsthand detail is the July 2021 newspaper; no 2024-26 visit or photo was found. The 1980 event year marks a decade, since the Register gives no year. A Facebook post by Missouri Conservation History (in search results only, not read) mentions a 2023 deed agreement; not used.
